claim: The10/24 initial assisted-recognition score shows exploratory evidence of category association under the global label-shuffle null. The7/24 adjacent score does not clear correction across the four planned checks.
paired_task_check: Preserving broad training pair, initial expected5.5 vs observed10, rawp.1875; adjacent expected6.5 vs observed7, rawp.5. Only16 shared pair swaps exist, so even the smallest possible unrandomized exact p is.0625; this check is weak and cannot establish an absence of within-pair discrimination.
interpretation: Some training-category signal, concentrated in initial fictional capitals and diets. No established reliable decoding of the next training task from adjacent checkpoint differences.
limitations: Exploratory post-hoc semantic judging by assistant already exposed to some results; no independent confirmation.
Eight fixed toy categories and three reused initialization seeds, not24 independent problems.
Label-exchangeability null is a conditional association benchmark, not actual random assignment of training tasks or evidence about a broad task population.
Within-pair null has only16 permutations; coarse p-values and limited power.
Above overall null can arise from recognizing broad training topics; it does not establish faithful factual explanations, causal selectivity, or reliability on every update.
multiple_testing: Holm adjustment across the two windows and two nulls,4 total. Correction only covers this named family of tests; it does not eliminate earlier exploratory selection or semantic-judge bias.
